quotes.text: Learn how to save Naira card to charge customers later.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: The customer must authorize the use of the local merchant of record service provider for future payments.
If the SetupIntent transitions from `requires_action` to `succeeded`, the setup is correct.
If the customer isn’t in a checkout flow for the current PaymentIntent, you must also set the `off_session` value to true.

findings: November keeps the purpose and replaces two full May sections with Checkout and Direct API links (raw/stripe-payments-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2026-11-07.md:5-14, raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:4-12,96-108). Diff line 397 combines the last removal and first addition because of source termination; the pinned raws resolve the fragments. The linked November bodies remain unread.

The summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:17 should distinguish written permission and terms from a Stripe Mandate payload and from explicit customer authorization of the local merchant-of-record provider. The May Checkout branch calls for an upfront opt-in and a retained written agreement. Off-session terms include scope, anticipated frequency/timing and amount determination, plus cancellation policy for subscriptions. Checkout requires authorizing the local provider for future payments (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:29-46,60-94). The Nigeria overview (raw/stripe-payments-countries-nigeria-2026-11-07.md:5-15,76-83,105-117) separately supplies partner identity, invite-request scope and the Naira card matrix, without proving account eligibility or a payment. Partner-MoR differs from Stripe Managed Payments (wiki/sources/source-stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:14-23; wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:8-14,40-42).

May Checkout creates a setup-mode Session for the Stripe Customer, which the merchant maps to its user. Test success is the SetupIntent transition from requires_action to succeeded (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:42-94). Direct API setup creates an ng_card SetupIntent with Customer and usage, passes the SetupIntent secret to browser Stripe.js, and shows confirmNgCardSetup with return_url and online infer_from_client (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:110-151,220-270). Separate charge-and-save starts/attempts a PaymentIntent with Customer, confirm and setup_future_usage=off_session, a return URL and optional mandate_data. Its sample includes explicit IP/user agent, NGN and automatic capture (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:332-370). These are distinct setup, payment and consent identities. The current summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:24,28-35 should scope the successful SetupIntent transition to the successful test/setup outcome and keep redirects distinct from that outcome.

The baseline wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:35 and wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:58-59 overstate a code sample as a mandate_data requirement. The May PaymentIntent prose explicitly says optional mandate_data (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:339-367), and the distinct November Create PaymentIntent reference says the object is optional and usable with confirm=true (raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:627-650). The May browser SetupIntent sample infers acceptance metadata from the client (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:248-265). A separately captured November Billing SetupIntents variant performs server confirmation with explicit IP and user agent in its example and then uses Stripe.js for the redirect/mandate authorization (raw/stripe-billing-subscriptions-ng-card-variant-c8486b9656-2026-11-07.md:36-58). Date and qualify by route/client-server role, retaining consumer's written permission regardless of optional request payload. The typed field, recorded permission and authorized mandate are separate.

In the manual redirect branch, require both PaymentIntent.status=requires_action and next_action.type=redirect_to_url, then take the redirect URL from that next_action. Browser return can include the PaymentIntent ID and client secret. Use server webhook status to verify payment outcome (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:272-330). The mapped source and reciprocal concept omit the status check and verification boundary (wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:37-39; wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:63-65). The later charge makes and confirms a new PaymentIntent using the saved PaymentMethod ID from the preceding Intent and its Customer, with off_session=true when the customer is absent. Server detach deactivates the reusable payment method and sends mandate.updated and payment_method.detached (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:372-396). The current summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:41-47 should distinguish conditional off_session and detach from payment outcomes or subscription cancellation.

source_assessments.reason: The baseline needs separate written and partner consent, optional versus example mandate fields, gated redirect and verified status, and conditional off-session behavior. November only adds navigation.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-card/set-up-future-payments says to save Naira cards for later charges and links Checkout and Direct API (new raw lines 5-14). May shows written customer permission with off-session terms, the app's mapping to a Stripe Customer and explicit authorization of the local merchant-of-record provider for future payments on the Checkout route. Its setup-mode Session invokes customer authentication and the successful test reaches SetupIntent succeeded from requires_action (old raw lines 29-94). Direct API saves without an initial charge using a server-created Customer-linked SetupIntent and browser confirmNgCardSetup with its client secret and mandate data. A separate PaymentIntent can attempt a charge while saving with setup_future_usage (old raw lines 110-151, 220-270 and 332-370). The merchant can later create a separate PaymentIntent using the saved PaymentMethod ID and Customer, setting off_session when the customer is absent, or detach the reusable method server-side, which generates two events (old raw lines 372-396). The existing source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md captures the route types but needs the partner permission, optional API payload, redirect verification and conditional off-session qualifications. Setup success does not establish a later payment.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-card/set-up-future-payments, new raw lines 5-14 retain the purpose and turn the May full variants into navigation. Keep the May 8 consent terms, Customer-linked Checkout setup and Direct API workflows, browser Stripe.js example, separate future PaymentIntent and detach semantics dated (old raw lines 29-94, 133-151, 220-270 and 372-396). Correct source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md and the reciprocal Nigeria concept so optional PaymentIntent mandate_data and the sample's explicit IP and user agent are kept distinct from browser SetupIntent infer_from_client and written authorization (old raw lines 248-265 and 339-367). The separate November Billing SetupIntent server-confirmation example also supplies explicit IP and user agent, reinforcing that this distinction applies by integration and confirmation route. Preserve both PaymentIntent requires_action and redirect_to_url checks and webhook verification (old raw lines 272-330). The separate Nigeria overview provides invite-request and partner-MoR context. These dated examples and links do not establish account access, changes to the unread variants, an authorized mandate from a redirect alone, completed payment or funds availability.
